analysis:
Examined three changed files; none touch the provider wire protocol, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, or prefix-cache storage.

1) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (new test at lines 181-203): a test-only addition checking that the prefill geometry rollback env keys (EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey) pass through LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment into the plist. It also asserts that WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys does not include them. The surrounding tests keep the passthrough allowlist behavior: UNRELATED_SECRET, PATH and HOME are excluded, and the Gemma config-backed keys are excluded. This does not widen the env surface in the tests, so it is consistent with TB-003 and no regression is evident. The production allowlist change itself (adding these keys to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys) is not in the supplied evidence. These keys are tuning knobs, not secrets. A local operator can already set env for their own provider (ADV-001 scope).

2) scripts/gemma_contbatch/config.py (lines 33-37): comment-only change documenting the raw scheduler prefill schema 5. No behavior change.

3) scripts/gemma_contbatch/validation.py (line 16): the benchmark validator now also accepts raw scheduler prefill schemaVersion 5. This is a dev-time benchmark script, outside the runtime trust boundaries. The existing model ID check, finite-value assertion and matrix checks are unchanged.

T-041 (cache) is not affected. Remaining question for integration: the Swift production changes that add the prefill chunk and step budget keys and bump the scheduler schema are outside this batch. If they alter engine or admission behavior (T-010 and T-029 availability, e.g. larger chunks holding the GPU longer), that should be reviewed there.
